description: The GC's split of the heap into gen 0, 1 and 2, where new objects start in gen 0 and only survivors are promoted, so most collections stay small and fast.
The heap area for objects of 85,000 bytes or more, collected only with gen 2 and rarely compacted.
The default GC mode for ASP.NET Core apps, which since .NET 9 adapts its number of heaps to the load through DATAS.
A stack-only `ref struct` view over contiguous memory that slices without copying and cannot be stored on the heap or held across an `await`.
A heap-storable counterpart of `Span<T>` for buffers that must live in fields or across asynchronous calls.
A shared pool of reusable arrays: `Rent` returns an array at least as long as requested and `Return` gives it back for reuse.
The standard .NET micro-benchmarking library, run in Release, whose `[MemoryDiagnoser]` reports allocated bytes and GC counts per operation.
